notes: Dev-split ABox revision (all determinate, no worlds): Sirius moves to Cygnus (brightest_star_in: functional, subproperty of located_in). The one related question reaches Sirius by its nickname, the Dog Star (binding, checked before editing), and asks its constellation through the subproperty; the nickname comes from Canis Major, so a model may be pulled back to the old answer by the name, which is what the binding tests. Derived: the celestial hemisphere by transitivity of located_in (Sirius in Cygnus, Cygnus in the north), whether Sirius and Deneb share a constellation (subproperty: a join of two located_in values), and the English meaning of the constellation's name (composition: greater dog or swan; text often glosses Canis Major as "the Greater Dog" next to Sirius, so the old answer is close to stored). Cygnus lies wholly in the northern celestial hemisphere, so the hemisphere answer flips cleanly. Residual risk: a model that stores Sirius's declination (about -17 degrees) holds a second route to "southern"; that stored value is a fact about Sirius and goes with its new place. Antares (Scorpius) is the near unrelated question (Orion was dropped, since Rigel and Betelgeuse both get named).
